comparison: Both evaluations support the experimental observation of viscosity behavior in zebrafish blastoderm (C1, C3, C11, C14, C31). OpenEval emphasizes the VFT behavior and experimental data from Figure 1C, while peer reviewers acknowledge this as the central phenomenon requiring explanation. Both find the claims well-supported.

Perfect agreement on the central mechanistic finding (C4, C5, C20, C21, C22, C43, C107, C108). Both evaluations support the explanation that cell overlap creates free area leading to viscosity saturation. OpenEval cites simulation data from Figure 5E, while peer reviewers find 'compelling evidence' for the polydispersity and softness mechanism.

Strong agreement on simulation reproduction of experimental observations (C18, C19, C40, C41, C118, C119). OpenEval highlights quantitative agreement with VFT fitting in Figure 2A, while peer reviewers accept the 'simplified model' and 'minimal active matter simulations' approach without concerns about quantitative reproduction.

Both evaluations support the facilitation mechanism (C23, C24, C25, C82, C83, C95, C96). OpenEval provides detailed evidence from Figure 3A and Videos 1-3, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the cooperative mechanisms involving 'active noise, particle softness and size heterogeneity cooperating.'

Complete agreement on absence of aging (C26, C27, C28, C112, C113, C114, C115). OpenEval cites Figure 6A-B showing independence from waiting time, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through their acceptance of the equilibrium treatment without raising concerns.

Both evaluations support the application of equilibrium concepts (C29, C50, C116, C117). OpenEval bases this on the absence of aging and successful equilibrium-based calculations, while peer reviewers explicitly accept 'a bridge between concepts from jamming of particulate systems and experiments' without challenging the equilibrium treatment.

Both evaluations support the dynamics from Fs(q,t) analysis (C63, C64, C65, C66, C67). OpenEval details the two-step decay and plateau behavior from Figure 2B-D, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these technical results supporting the main viscosity findings.

Strong agreement on heterogeneous dynamics at single-cell level (C69, C70, C71, C72, C76, C77, C78). OpenEval emphasizes the eight orders of magnitude variation in relaxation times from Figure 3A, while peer reviewers accept the overall mechanism without questioning the dynamical heterogeneity findings.

Both evaluations support the validation and breakdown of theoretical predictions (C85, C87, C88). OpenEval shows Gaussian fit validity below φS and deviation above from Figure 3C-D, while peer reviewers accept the glass-like behavior characterization and transition without challenge.

Both evaluations support the overlap analysis (C92, C93, C94). OpenEval details distributions from Figure 4A-B and connection to free area creation, while peer reviewers accept cell overlap mechanism through their acceptance that 'softness of cells' contributes to the phenomenon. OpenEval also addresses C101, C103-C105 in R11.

Both evaluations support the Voronoi tessellation analysis (C99-C106). OpenEval provides detailed support from Figure 5B-D for distributions and negative Afree interpretation, while peer reviewers accept the quantitative characterization of cell overlap and free area creation without questioning the Voronoi analysis.

Both evaluations support the control simulations and model selection (C32, C33, C34, C35). OpenEval cites monodisperse crystallization and binary mixture results from appendices, while peer reviewers affirm the necessity of both polydispersity and softness through their statement about 'compelling evidence.'

Perfect agreement on modeling choices (C54, C55, C56). OpenEval finds reasonable justification for timescale arguments and 2D choice, while peer reviewers accept the 'simplified model' and 'minimal active matter simulations' approach without challenging these simplifications.

Both evaluations support the stress relaxation characterization (C61). OpenEval documents two-step decay from Figure 7A-B, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this technical result through their acceptance of the overall viscosity calculations.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about 3D results (C45). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of detailed data and figures, while peer reviewers explicitly note 'It will be interesting in the future to see whether and how the findings change when considering 3D tissues,' indicating this remains an open question.

Divergent evaluations on adhesion effects (C46, C47, C48, C49). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are speculative without direct supporting evidence from the study. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the absence of explicit adhesion forces as reasonable for the minimal model approach.

Both evaluations support experimental polydispersity observations (C30, C34, C17). OpenEval cites Figure 1B and Appendix 1-figure 1D, while peer reviewers accept polydispersity as a necessary feature through their affirmation of the overall mechanism. Partial overlap with R8 on C34.

Both evaluations support soft interaction modeling (C35, C16, C90, C91). OpenEval justifies this by experimental evidence of cell overlap, while peer reviewers accept softness as contributing to the phenomenon. Partial overlap with R8 on C35.

OpenEval supports structural properties from simulations (C36, C37) with evidence from Figure 1D-E showing mixing and g(r) with short-range peaks. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific structural characterization claims.

OpenEval supports comparison to other systems (C68) citing Gnan and Zaccarelli, 2019. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this comparative claim about unique behavior of polydisperse cell systems.

OpenEval supports prior work context and aging test motivation (C109, C110, C111) citing Philippe et al., 2018. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about prior work and logical predictions.
OpenEval supports summary of relevant prior work (C6, C7, C8, C9, C10, C15) with multiple citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background and context claims.

OpenEval supports comparison to glass-forming materials (C2) based on VFT fitting and established glass physics knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparative claim.

OpenEval supports broader significance claims (C42, C44) about free area explanation and equilibrium PT link. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific significance and interpretation claims.
OpenEval supports model component descriptions (C57, C59) with citations and methods details. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific model definition claims.
OpenEval supports interpretation of aging results (C53) as logically consistent with data and timescale arguments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific interpretive claim.
